# Clementine Ainslie

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046)</sub>
- **Role:** Music teacher  <sub>[v1 c17 P20](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0020), [v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046)</sub>

## Appearance

Clementine is a tall, stately, and exceptionally beautiful woman with fair skin, a fine nose, and blue eyes. Her glossy hair, described as the shade of molasses taffy, is worn in smooth, tight braids around her head. She possesses a gentle, serene smile with dimples, giving her a youthful, charming look.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 c5 P8](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0008), [v5 c6 P4](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0004), [v5 c8 P28](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0028), [v5 c13 P14](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0014)_

## Personality

Clementine is gentle, sweet, and patient, possessing an intuitive understanding of others and an enduring capacity for love and forgiveness. Though generally calm and soft-spoken, she has a firm sense of propriety and can display a spark of temper when pushed too far. She enjoys poetry and music, and maintains a youthful, romantic spirit despite past heartbreaks.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 c5 P12](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0012), [v5 c5 P17](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0017), [v5 c5 P28](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0028), [v5 c6 P4](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0004), [v5 c8 P28](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0028), [v5 c13 P14](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0014), [v5 c13 P31](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0031)_

- Gentle and patient  <sub>[v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 c6 P4](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0004)</sub>

## Goals

- To give and receive affection and comfort others  <sub>[v5 c5 P12](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0012), [v5 c6 P4](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0004)</sub>

## History

Clementine Ainslie grew up in Glen St. Agnes with her mother and older sister, Harriet. At age seventeen, she fell in love with Martin Crawford, but he was lost at sea, leaving her heartbroken. Following her mother's death, Clementine made a solemn vow on her mother's Bible never to marry so her sister would not be left alone. Years later, she began teaching music lessons, including to Nell Harcourt's daughters, and became a beloved figure among the local children. She eventually met the widowed minister, Rev. John Ashdown, at a secluded forest spring, and a quiet courtship developed between them. Although she initially felt bound by her vow to refuse his marriage proposal, her sister Harriet ultimately released her from the promise. Clementine accepted Mr. Ashdown's proposal, bringing warmth and care to the minister's neglected household.

_Sources: [v1 c17 P20](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0020), [v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 c6 P4](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0004), [v5 c6 P13](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0013), [v5 c6 P14](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0014), [v5 c6 P22](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0022), [v5 c6 P23](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0023), [v5 c6 P24](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0024), [v5 c13 P1](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0001), [v5 c13 P5](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0005), [v5 c13 P19](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0019), [v5 c13 P20](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0020), [v5 c13 P28](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0028), [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018), [v5 c14 P28](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0028), [v5 c14 P34](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0034)_

- Her father died when she was three years old, leaving her to be raised by her mother and older sister Harriet  <sub>[v5 c6 P13](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0013), [v5 c6 P14](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0014)</sub>
- Was engaged at seventeen to Martin Crawford, who tragically drowned at sea  <sub>[v5 c6 P13](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0013), [v5 c6 P14](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0014), [v5 c13 P1](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0001)</sub>
